verdict.rationale: Steel publishes an open-source steel-browser repo with a pre-built Docker image (API + UI) that controls Chrome via CDP, and agents can connect to it with Puppeteer, Playwright or Selenium. That implies a self-hosted local browser the product itself provides. However, no evidence explicitly documents running it on a local machine without a cloud account, and the agent-framework integrations are all described as running on Steel cloud sessions. Missing for 10: explicit docs for local/self-hosted setup without an account, evidence that the CLI and integrations can target a local instance, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the agent against a local browser on my own machine for development, without any cloud account

citations.quote: Uses Puppeteer and CDP for complete control over Chrome instances -- allowing you to connect using Puppeteer, Playwright, or Selenium.
Steel is the open-source browser API for AI agents
